text_blocks.snippet: Hospital-acquired pressure injuries (HAPIs), also known as pressure ulcers, are a significant concern, both clinically and financially. They can lead to increased patient suffering, longer hospital stays, and substantial costs for healthcare systems. Estimates of the cost of HAPIs range from $10,708 to $129,248 per patient. In the US, the total cost of HAPIs is estimated to be in the billions of dollars annually.
Here's a breakdown of the costs associated with HAPIs:

list.snippet: A single Stage 1 pressure ulcer can cost around $418, according to OP2 Labs.
A Stage 2 pressure ulcer can cost around $3,674, according to OP2 Labs.
A Stage 3 pressure ulcer can cost around $8,741, according to OP2 Labs.
A Stage 4 pressure ulcer can cost up to $44,000, according to OP2 Labs.
Some studies show costs can be even higher, ranging from $20,900 to $151,700 per pressure ulcer, according to Relias.
The average cost of HAPI care can be around $10,708, according to the National Institutes of Health (NIH).
HAPIs increase the length of hospital stays, contributing to higher overall costs.
Medicare estimates that each pressure ulcer adds an extra $43,180 to a hospital stay, according to the Agency for Healthcare Research and Quality (AHRQ).
Due to the high costs associated with HAPIs, Medicare and other payers often do not reimburse hospitals for these costs, putting further financial strain on healthcare facilities.
The estimated annual cost of HAPIs in the US is in the billions of dollars, with some estimates exceeding $26.8 billion, according to Healthcare Finance News.
One study estimated that the cost of treating HAPIs in the US could reach $26.8 billion, according to the National Institutes of Health (NIH).

Another study focused on Australian public hospitals estimated that the total cost of pressure injuries, including both direct and indirect costs, was $1,516.7 million for Stage 1 injuries and $954.5 million for Stage 3 injuries.
HAPIs can lead to lawsuits, with average settlements around $250,000 and some awards exceeding $312 million, according to WoundVision.
HAPIs can also lead to lost productivity for patients and their families.
The cost of treating pressure ulcers also depends on factors like the severity of the wound, complications, and length of stay.
